audience.programmeDescription: VU Notarial Law develops legal analysis and preventive advice about property, family, inheritance and business relationships. Students build a broad legal foundation before advanced Dutch private and tax law, notarial practice, pleading and an independent legal thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers comparative private law, transnational business law and negotiation. VU develops these areas through a longer Dutch-law sequence covering property, inheritance, family property, company law, taxation and notarial practice. The related UCR courses cover parts of that sequence.

curriculum.limitation: All 180 EC are compulsory. The plan follows the revised curriculum for September 2026 entrants, with no minor space. Professional identity and Dutch language requirements add no credits. Thesis entry requires 120 EC including Legal Skills. Pleading requires 99 EC including Legal Skills.

componentNotes.y1-legal-skills: Students must meet the professional identity and Dutch language requirements.
componentNotes.y2-admin: Students must complete introductory administrative law and meet the second-year professional identity requirement.
componentNotes.y3-thesis: Students complete a 6 EC independent legal thesis.
componentNotes.y3-pleading: Students can choose the notarial conflict resolution option within this course.
